examples.problem:
Given that the minor of $a_{23}$ is $5,$ find all the possible values of $k$ in the matrix
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14075201/assets/1d37ba9039f24a96be2d148c9f30c8a10ca30c9745ad8a28df23de5a42f6dcab.png)
examples.worked_solution:
First, we remove the second row and third column:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14075201/assets/80f9b95139f7b571c7752ee1feec4c9d3df8456223581736ae019344a6f9a080.png)

The minor of $a_{23}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}det[\begin{aligned}k & 3 \\ -1 & 2k\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}k & 3 \\ -1 & 2k\end{aligned}| \\  & =k\cdot 2k-3\cdot (-1) \\  & =2{k}^{2}+3.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that the minor of $a_{23}$ is $5,$ so we must have:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{k}^{2}+3 & =5 \\ 2{k}^{2} & =2 \\ {k}^{2} & =1 \\ k & =\pm 1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $k=-1$ and $k=1.$

feedback.problem:
For the matrix
$B=[\begin{aligned}2p & q & 3 \\ 1 & 4p & 5 \\ 6 & 7 & 2q\end{aligned}],$
find the minor ${M}_{23}$ of the element ${b}_{23}.$

${M}_{23}=${{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
To evaluate the minor of ${b}_{23},$ we remove the second row and third column:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}2p & q & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & 5 \\ 6 & 7 & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor of ${b}_{23}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{23} & =det[\begin{aligned}2p & q \\ 6 & 7\end{aligned}] \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2p & q \\ 6 & 7\end{aligned}| \\  & =(2p)\cdot 7-q\cdot 6 \\  & =14p-6q.\end{aligned}
$$
